questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a magnetic material?
questions.explanation: Copper is not a magnetic material. Only iron, cobalt, nickel, and their alloys (such as steel) are attracted to magnets.

questions.stem: What happens when two north poles of magnets are brought together?
questions.explanation: Like poles repel each other. Two north poles (or two south poles) will push apart, while a north and south pole will attract.

questions.stem: In which direction do magnetic field lines travel outside a magnet?

options.text: From north pole to south pole
From south pole to north pole

questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines travel from the north pole to the south pole outside the magnet. They form closed loops, continuing from south to north inside the magnet.

questions.stem: What happens if you cut a bar magnet in half?

options.text: You get an isolated north pole and an isolated south pole
You get two smaller magnets, each with both a north and south pole
One half becomes stronger and the other becomes weaker

questions.explanation: Magnetic poles always come in pairs. Cutting a magnet in half creates two smaller magnets, each with its own north and south pole. You cannot create an isolated magnetic pole.

questions.stem: What do closely spaced magnetic field lines indicate?
questions.explanation: Closely spaced field lines indicate a stronger magnetic field. The field is strongest at the poles of a magnet, where the lines are closest together.

options.text: A magnet that only works at very low temperatures
A magnet created by passing electric current through a wire
A magnet that is always magnetic and keeps its magnetism permanently
A material that becomes magnetic when placed near a permanent magnet but loses its magnetism when removed

questions.explanation: An induced magnet is a magnetic material that becomes temporarily magnetised when placed near a permanent magnet. It loses most of its magnetism when the permanent magnet is removed.

questions.stem: Why does a compass needle point north?

options.text: Because Earth's geographic north pole is a magnetic north pole
Because the sun's radiation pushes it north
Because of gravity pulling it northward
Because the north-seeking pole of the compass is attracted to Earth's magnetic south pole, which is near geographic north

questions.explanation: Earth's magnetic south pole is located near the geographic North Pole. The north-seeking pole of a compass is attracted to this magnetic south pole, which is why the compass points towards geographic north.
